To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
leukotriene receptor antagonism attenuates bronchoconstriction induced by cold-air ISH.
LY171883, an antagonist of LTD4 activity via LTD receptors, increased the respiratory heat loss required for 20% fall in FEV1 by cold air ISH.
LY171883, an LTD4 antagonist, increased the PD20RHL in asthmatics during cold-air ISHV, and this effect was more marked in more reactive subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of leukotrienes on cold-air-induced bronchospasm in asthmatics.
the effects of LY171883 on bronchoconstriction induced by cold air ISH.
the effect of LY171883, an LTD4 receptor antagonist, on the cold-air-induced bronchospasm of asthmatics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LTD4 plays a small role in cold-air-induced airway narrowing in asthmatics.
LY171883, at a dose of 600 mg twice daily for 2 wk, did not affect baseline FEV1, but did increase the PD20RHL and PD20VE in cold-air ISH.
LY171883 does not completely block the effects of LTD4 during cold-air-induced bronchospasm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leukotriene antagonism may have a role in the therapy of asthma.
LY171883, an LTD4 receptor antagonist, attenuated cold-air ISH-induced bronchoconstriction.
LY171883 is a useful agent for the treatment of asthma, but it is not a useful agent for determining the mechanism of cold-air-induced bronchospasm in asthmatics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leukotriene pathway is involved in the pathogenesis of cold air-induced bronchospasm.
the leukotrienes may play a significant role in airway hyperresponsiveness to cold air.
leukotriene receptor blockade may reduce bronchospastic responses to cold air.
